response.title: Can a solar panel and power station run a small pond pump all day, and what size do I need?
response.answer:
Yes! A solar panel and portable power station can run a small pond pump 24 hours a day, including overnight, as long as the solar panel generates enough energy during daylight and the power station stores enough for nighttime use.

For a typical small pond pump using 10–30 watts, I'd start with a 200W solar panel and a 1,000Wh LiFePO₄ power station. That's a reasonable starting setup, although winter weather and cloudy days may require more solar capacity.

The most important factor is your pump's actual power consumption, measured in watts (W).

markup:
**Yes! A solar panel and portable power station can run a small pond pump 24 hours a day**, including overnight, as long as the solar panel generates enough energy during daylight and the power station stores enough for nighttime use.

For a typical small pond pump using 10–30 watts, I'd start with a **200W solar panel and a 1,000Wh LiFePO₄ power station**. That's a reasonable starting setup, although winter weather and cloudy days may require more solar capacity.

## 1. What size solar panel and battery do you need?

The most important factor is your pump's actual power consumption, measured in watts (W).

| Pump power | Energy used per day | Suggested solar panel | Suggested battery |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 5W | 120Wh | 50–100W | 300Wh |
| 10W | 240Wh | 100–150W | 500Wh |
| 20W | 480Wh | 200–300W | 1,000Wh |
| 30W | 720Wh | 300–400W | 1,500Wh |
| 50W | 1,200Wh | 500–600W | 2,000Wh |

These are approximate sizes for continuous operation with around four effective peak-sun-hours per day and allowance for system losses. They're not guarantees for winter or extended cloudy weather.

## 2. How the system works

<box gap={2}>
  <grid columns={3} gap={2}>
    <grid-item>
      <AsyncImage query="portable folding solar panel outdoors in sunlight 200 watt" aspectRatio="5:4" shop_eligible={true}/>
      <text weight="medium" size="sm" textAlign="center">Solar panel</text>
      <caption textAlign="center">Generates daytime power</caption>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <AsyncImage query="portable LiFePO4 power station 1000Wh battery solar generator outdoors" aspectRatio="5:4" shop_eligible={true}/>
      <text weight="medium" size="sm" textAlign="center">Power station</text>
      <caption textAlign="center">Stores energy overnight</caption>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <AsyncImage query="small submersible pond water fountain pump water flowing garden pond" aspectRatio="5:4" shop_eligible={true}/>
      <text weight="medium" size="sm" textAlign="center">Pond pump</text>
      <caption textAlign="center">Runs continuously</caption>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
  <row justify="center" align="center" gap={2}>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Solar panel</text>
    <icon name="arrow-right" color="secondary"/>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Power station</text>
    <icon name="arrow-right" color="secondary"/>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Pump</text>
  </row>
</box>

Make sure the power station supports **simultaneous solar charging and powering the pump**, and automatically continues supplying power when sunlight disappears.

## 3. Calculate your exact setup

Adjust these values to see the recommended system size.

{@body const [watts,setWatts] = DIL.useState(20)}
{@body const [sun,setSun] = DIL.useState(4)}
{@body const [backup,setBackup] = DIL.useState(1)}
{@body const daily=watts*24}
{@body const panel=Math.ceil(daily/(sun*0.75)/50)*50}
{@body const battery=Math.ceil(daily*backup/(0.85*0.9)/100)*100}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    **Pump power**
    <title size="lg" color="default" tabularNums>{watts} W</title>
  </row>
  <slider min={5} max={100} step={5} value={watts} onChange={setWatts}/>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    **Effective sun hours per day**
    <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{sun} hours</text>
  </row>
  <slider min={2} max={6} step={0.5} value={sun} onChange={setSun}/>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    **Battery backup without solar**
    <text weight="medium" tabularNums>{backup} {backup===1?"day":"days"}</text>
  </row>
  <slider min={0.5} max={3} step={0.5} value={backup} onChange={setBackup}/>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <grid columns={2} gap={3}>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Suggested solar array</text>
      <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{panel}W</title>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <text color="secondary" size="xs">Suggested battery</text>
      <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>{battery.toLocaleString()}Wh</title>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
  <text color="secondary" size="sm">Daily pump consumption: {daily}Wh. Estimates assume 75% effective solar output and approximately 76.5% usable battery-to-load energy. Actual power station idle consumption and weather may increase requirements.</text>
</box>

Sizing for the least sunny month, rather than the annual average, is important for year-round operation. <Cite refs={["turn595256search13","turn595256search12"]}/>

Also, for a pond, consider a low-power DC pump to avoid unnecessary AC inverter losses. Keep the power station sheltered from rain and splashes, use outdoor-rated connections, and ensure the pump can restart automatically after an outage.

## 4. Two questions to get the right size

{@body const [pump,setPump] = DIL.useState("20")}
{@body const [location,setLocation] = DIL.useState("Sunnyvale, California")}
{@body const [season,setSeason] = DIL.useState("year-round")}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <form gap={3} onSubmit={()=>GenUI.issueNewTurn("Size a solar panel and power station for my "+pump+"W pond pump running 24 hours daily in "+location+", "+season+". Recommend suitable capacity for local sunlight and weather.")}>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>How many watts does your pond pump use?</label>
      <input value={pump} onChange={setPump} placeholder="e.g. 20" required/>
    </box>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>Where will the pond be located?</label>
      <input value={location} onChange={setLocation} required/>
    </box>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>When should it operate?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={season} onChange={setSeason}>
        <radio value="year-round">Year-round, including winter</radio>
        <radio value="spring through fall">Spring through fall only</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <button block submit>Calculate my setup <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>

With those details, I can narrow down the solar panel wattage, battery capacity, and whether a smaller, less expensive setup will work.
